sd.name: South Dakota
sd.pollHours: 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time (South Dakota has two time zones, Central and Mountain)

early.text: You can vote in person at your county auditor's office with a photo ID. This started September 18 and runs until at least 5 p.m. on Monday, November 2.

mail.text: Your mail ballot must reach your county election office on Election Day in time to be taken to your voting precinct before the polls close at 7 p.m. local time. A postmark does not count, so with so little time left it is safer to hand-deliver it to your county auditor's office.

registration.text: The registration deadline was Monday, October 19 at 5 p.m. local time, which is 15 days before Election Day. The official sources do not list same-day registration.

sd.note: The state absentee page says you 'may be eligible' if you cannot go to your polling place, but it does not clearly say whether you need a reason, so mail.noExcuse is null. The same page says anyone registered can vote in person at the auditor's office once absentee voting starts. The request deadline for a mailed ballot is 5 p.m. on Nov 2 (official calendar), but a ballot requested this late will almost certainly not make it back in time, so voters should go in person. A voter confined by sickness or disability can send an authorized messenger until 3 p.m. on Election Day. Ballots delivered after the polls close are not counted.

tn.name: Tennessee
tn.pollHours: Opening time depends on the county. All polls close at 7 p.m. Central or 8 p.m. Eastern. Anyone in line at closing can still vote.

early.text: Early voting runs Wednesday, October 14 through Thursday, October 29. That means this week is your last chance to vote early. Hours and places depend on your county.

mail.text: Tennessee only lets people vote by mail for certain reasons, such as being 60 or older, being sick or disabled, or being out of the county the whole voting period. The ballot must reach your county election office by the time polls close on Election Day. You must return it by mail or delivery service. Handing it in at an early voting site or polling place is not allowed. The request deadline was October 24.

registration.text: The registration deadline was Monday, October 5, 2026. Tennessee does not offer same-day registration.

tn.note: You need a photo ID to vote in person; student IDs and out-of-state licenses are not accepted. The poll-hours wording comes from the state's August 2026 election release; the state calendar does not list November poll hours, so check your county's hours in the GoVoteTN app. The state calendar does not mention same-day registration anywhere; the registration deadline is the cutoff.

tx.name: Texas
tx.pollHours: 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. at all polling places statewide (local time; El Paso area is on Mountain Time)

early.text: Early voting is Monday, October 19 through Friday, October 30. You can vote at any early voting site in your county. Hours differ by site.

mail.text: Texas only lets some people vote by mail: age 65 or older, sick or disabled, out of the county the whole voting period, expecting a baby within three weeks, or in jail. A ballot with no postmark must arrive by 7 p.m. on Election Day. A ballot postmarked by 7 p.m. on Election Day can arrive until 5 p.m. on Wednesday, November 4. You can also hand-deliver it to your county early voting clerk's office on Election Day.

registration.text: The registration deadline was Monday, October 5, 2026. Texas does not offer same-day registration.

tx.note: Postmarks can be late: the state warns USPS sometimes postmarks mail a day after you drop it off. Ask for a free hand postmark at a post office counter. The application deadline for a mail ballot was October 23, so only people who already have a ballot can use mail now. On Election Day, some counties let you vote at any site (vote centers) and others make you use your own precinct, so check your county. Bring one of the seven accepted photo IDs.

ut.name: Utah

early.text: In-person early voting is October 20 through October 30. Every county offers it, but days, hours and places differ, so check with your county clerk.

mail.text: Active registered voters are mailed a ballot automatically. Your county clerk must have your ballot by 8 p.m. on Election Day, November 3. A postmark does not count. You can also use an official drop box until 8 p.m. on Election Day.

registration.sameDayText: You can register in person during early voting or on Election Day at a vote center. Bring two forms of valid ID, including proof of where you live.
registration.text: Online and mail registration closed Friday, October 23 at 5 p.m. You can still register in person during early voting or on Election Day.

ut.note: Big trap: Utah no longer counts postmarks. A ballot that is mailed on or before Election Day but arrives later is not counted. Mail by now is risky; use a drop box or take it to your clerk. Drop boxes close at 8 p.m. The last day to request a replacement mail ballot was October 27 at 5 p.m. The early voting dates (Oct 20 to Oct 30) come from the state voter pamphlet and calendar; counties set their own hours.

vt.name: Vermont
vt.pollHours: Each town opens its polls between 5 a.m. and 10 a.m. All polls close at 7 p.m.

early.text: You can vote early in person at your town or city clerk's office during its business hours. Early voting starts 45 days before the election or as soon as ballots are ready in your town.

mail.text: Active voters were mailed a ballot automatically. To be safe, your town clerk should have it before the clerk's office closes on Monday, November 2. You can also bring your ballot to your polling place before 7 p.m. on Election Day or drop it in your town's drop box.

registration.sameDayText: You can register up to and including Election Day. Register at your town or city clerk's office during business hours before Election Day, or at your polling place on Election Day. First-time voters who register online or by mail must include a copy of an ID such as a driver's license, utility bill or bank statement.
registration.text: Vermont has no registration deadline. You can register any day through Election Day.

vt.note: The state page lists the mail-return deadline as the clerk's office closing time the day before the election, not the end of Election Day. It does not give a date for how late a mailed ballot can arrive, so mail it right away or hand it in. If you lost your ballot or did not get it, you can still vote at the polls by signing an Affidavit of No Ballot Cast. The 'start' date for early voting (Sept 19) is 45 days before Nov 3; the state says towns may start as soon as ballots are ready.

va.name: Virginia
va.pollHours: 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. Anyone in line at 7 p.m. can still vote.

early.text: Anyone registered can vote early in person at their local registrar's office or an early voting site. It ends at 5 p.m. on Saturday, October 31. Hours and places differ by locality, so call your registrar.

mail.text: Anyone can vote by mail without giving a reason. A mailed ballot must be postmarked by Election Day and arrive at your registrar's office by noon on Friday, November 6. You can also hand it in at the registrar's office, a drop-off site during early voting, or your polling place on Election Day (by 7 p.m.). The request deadline was October 23.

registration.sameDayText: After October 23 you can still register in person at your registrar's office or an early voting site, or at your polling place on Election Day. You vote a provisional ballot, which is counted after election officials check that you are eligible.
registration.text: The regular registration deadline was Friday, October 23. After that you can still register and vote with a provisional ballot.

va.note: A mailed ballot with no postmark may not be counted, so take it inside a post office and ask for a postmark, or hand-deliver it. People who register after the Oct 23 deadline vote on a provisional ballot, which takes extra steps to count. A first-time mail voter who registered by mail may need to include a copy of an ID with the ballot. The state's same-day registration page still mentions an October 24 date from an older election; the current 2026 deadline on the Upcoming Elections page is October 23.

wa.name: Washington
wa.pollHours: There are no neighborhood polling places. Official drop boxes and voting centers close at 8 p.m. on Election Day. Voting center hours differ by county.

early.text: Voting centers in each county are open from 18 days before Election Day (October 16) until 8 p.m. on Election Day. You can register, get a replacement ballot, or vote there. Hours differ by county.

mail.text: Every registered voter was mailed a ballot by October 16. Put it in an official drop box by 8 p.m. on Election Day, or mail it with a postmark dated no later than November 3. Mailed ballots must arrive by the close of business on the day before your county certifies results (Nov 23 for counties that certify Nov 24).

registration.sameDayText: You can register or update your registration in person at your county elections office or voting center until 8 p.m. on Election Day.
registration.text: The online and mail registration deadline is today, Monday, October 26. After that, register in person at a voting center until 8 p.m. on Election Day.

wa.note: The state says USPS recommends mailing your ballot at least a week before Election Day (October 27), and postmarks are not always applied the same day, so use a drop box now. Meter stamps or dated postage do not count as a postmark. The last-arrival date of Nov 23 comes from state rule WAC 434-250-120 ('day before certification') together with the state fact sheet's Nov 24 certification date; individual counties may certify on different days. Washington has no early-voting window in the usual sense: voting centers are the in-person option.

wv.name: West Virginia

early.text: Early voting is Wednesday, October 21 through Saturday, October 31 at your county courthouse, an annex or another site your county picks. Hours vary by county, with Saturday hours usually 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.

mail.text: You need an allowed reason to vote by mail, such as being sick, disabled, or away from your county for the whole voting period. Your application must reach your county clerk by October 28. Your ballot must be postmarked by Election Day and reach the clerk before the county vote count starts (November 9 on the state calendar). If you hand-deliver it, it must be at the clerk's office by Monday, November 2.

registration.text: The registration deadline was Tuesday, October 13, 2026. West Virginia does not offer same-day registration for most voters.

wv.note: A mailed absentee ballot with no postmark can still count if it arrives by Wednesday, November 4. Because USPS may not postmark right away, mail it early or hand-deliver it. The state calendar lists November 9 as when postmarked ballots are accepted, tied to the start of the county canvass (vote count review); treat it as the outside limit and do not wait. Emergency absentee ballots are available October 27 to noon on November 3 for people who become confined by illness or injury or are in the hospital. Only a few special groups can register late. You need a photo ID to vote in person.

wi.name: Wisconsin
wi.pollHours: 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Anyone in line by 8 p.m. can vote.

early.text: In-person absentee voting at your municipal clerk's office or other site runs from October 20 at the earliest to Sunday, November 1 at the latest. Each town sets its own days and hours, and some stop earlier, so call your clerk.

mail.text: Any registered voter can vote by mail with no reason. Your ballot must be in the hands of election officials by 8 p.m. on Election Day. A postmark does not count. The online or mail request deadline is 5 p.m. on Thursday, October 29. You can drop it off at your clerk's office, polling place, or drop box if your town has one.

registration.sameDayText: You can register at your polling place on Election Day. Bring proof of where you live (for example a lease or utility bill), and bring your photo ID because you need it to get a ballot. You can also register in person at your clerk's office until the Friday before the election (Oct 30) at 5 p.m. or closing.
registration.text: The online and mail registration deadline was Wednesday, October 14. You can still register in person.

wi.note: You cannot ask for a ballot in person and take it home: in-person absentee ballots are voted in the clerk's office. Mailing a ballot now is risky because postmarks do not count; hand-deliver it. The 8 p.m. closing time comes from the state calendar and an August 2026 state reminder. You need a photo ID to vote. If you moved within Wisconsin in the last 28 days, you may have to vote from your old address.

wy.name: Wyoming

early.text: You can vote in person at your county clerk's office from October 6 through Monday, November 2. This is called absentee voting, but you can do it in person.

mail.text: Any registered voter can ask for an absentee ballot, with no reason needed, but not on Election Day itself. Your county clerk must have your ballot by 7 p.m. on Election Day. Late ballots are not counted. Mail can take up to seven days, so hand-delivering it to the clerk is safer now.

registration.sameDayText: You can register and vote at your polling place on Election Day. You can also register in person at the county clerk's office and vote absentee from October 20 to November 2. Bring proof of citizenship and proof of Wyoming residency.
registration.text: Normal registration closed Monday, October 19. You can still register at your county clerk's office or at your polling place on Election Day.

wy.note: The state's 2026 voter guide says mail or in-person registration closes 'not less than 14 days' before the election, while the state's Key Election Dates and calendar list October 19 (15 days). Either way, same-day registration at the polls is available. You must show an accepted photo ID to vote in person. A voter who moved counties must re-register in the new county.
